THE_FINDING.headline: The cascade can see the exotics precisely because it fails to reach the Standard Model.
chain: the only charges separating the exotics from a generation are psi and chi -- the two u(1)s the SM does not have
the SM group has rank 4; the cascade's Levi has rank 6; descending to the SM means shedding exactly psi and chi
at rank 4 the separation is gone EXACTLY: Dbar = d^c, H_d = L, S = nu^c as gauge multiplets
THE_FINDING.conclusion: the two u(1)s the cascade cannot shed (banked: centralizers preserve rank; no centralizer construction reaches rank 4 with a complex 27) are exactly the two u(1)s that distinguish the eleven exotics from a generation. The cascade's surplus rank is not only its defect; it is also its entire resolving power on this question. The exotics are not invisible to the cascade -- they are invisible to the SM.
THE_FINDING.second_order_reading_flagged_as_a_readin: what the cascade resolves is a SPLIT, not a LABEL: it sees eleven pieces but does not from the Levi alone say which nine states are matter. The tie is broken by z1, the one descent charge B876 records as object-supplied rather than imposed. Object supplies the split; the imposed charges supply the multiplet carving.
what_this_does_not_say: it does not make the exotics heavy -- that is the 27 VEV input, already closed as L133/L138 (the scout's R2/R3 pins the unique direction to S = omega_1)
the three so(10)s of the ambiguity are reachable by ADJOINT (78) directions -- rank-preserving centralisers, costing no 27 VEV. Making the exotics heavy costs a 27 VEV. Two different operations.
